title: Locate actual population classes with fixed coverability tables and binary counts
statement: Precompute E0C’s finite hierarchy, the backward-coverability basis for every core, and bases for each single-coordinate target x_i>=K. Binary comparisons of initial counts with these finitely many minimal vectors decide core access. If no core is reachable, a failed coordinate test selects a coordinate bounded throughout the actual class and its corresponding finite-control child. At a core node, stored bounded physical normalization words give base control and an explicit lattice-coset representative; HNF membership in the actual, possibly nonsaturated lattice distinguishes normalized buffered representatives. Recurse through at most d coordinates. All tables and words are paid finite fixed-input preprocessing, so class-location work is polynomial in variable binary population length at fixed network. This decides support membership, not factorial-weight normalization or sampling. Countercontrols: conditioning independent Poisson(V) counts on A+B=1 accepts with probability 2V exp(-2V), despite a fair coin sampling that class; event simulation for A+B=V pays numeric-V reaction activity. The later full binary equilibrium-sampler question is open.
